doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Master's degree at Teachers College and meeting his wife
summary: Raph explains why he did the master's, how it helped his credibility and writing, and how he met his wife there.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: You decided to get another degree.

I decided to get the master’s, after getting the bachelor’s, just simply because I was doing shows at that time and I had the time. I think I was doing a Broadway show that looked like it was going to last for a while, I forget which one it was, but it was on the books for about a year or so, so I went to Teacher’s College and horse traded my way into a degree.

It’s paid off insofar as it gives me a little credibility as far as knowing what I talk about educationally and instrument wise and all of that. I have a number of publications on the market, mostly through Carl Fisher, and in writing my bio in the books I’m able to naturally state that I have this degree and that degree, which means a lot with a lot of teachers. I also developed the vocabulary in taking education degrees to reach students a little bit better than I might have otherwise. It was just — that was the field that I thought I should get a little extended education in. I started for a doctorate and at that point I looked in the mirror and I thought come on, a doctorate, yeah, right, no I’m not going to do that. So I took two courses and that was it. But that’s how I met Mary Ann and we started going out together and ultimately got married. I met her at Teacher’s College. I was teaching there actually. I had a class where I had to teach all the instruments. And
she was the only student. They let her take the class. So naturally one thing led to another and we’ve been married now 23 years.
